2607.11197.title: What We Talk About When We Talk About LLM Planning: Evidence for Two Distinct Planning Abilities
2607.11197.paper_summary: When LLMs exhibit uneven performance across planning tasks, these gaps are often attributed to task difficulty. We argue that this explanation is incomplete, as task-level variation may reflect distinct latent planning competencies rather than differences along a single ability spectrum. We study this question on ACPBench-Hard by evaluating multiple LLM families under varying test-time reasoning budgets and applying a multidimensional item response theory model to uncover the latent competency structure underlying LLM planning. The analysis reveals two principal dimensions that shape planning performance: operational reasoning, the ability to evaluate local action applicability and immediate state transitions, and structural enumeration, the ability to reason about goal reachability and landmark structure. Operational reasoning improving under model scaling and longer reasoning traces, while structural enumeration remains comparatively insensitive. Our findings motivate competency-level evaluation of LLM planning, shifting the focus from whether models improve overall to which planning competencies improve, under what conditions, and why.
2607.11197.paper_summary_zh: 當大型語言模型（LLMs）在規劃任務中表現不均時，這些差距通常被歸因於任務的難度。我們認為這一解釋是不完整的，因為任務層面的變異可能反映出不同的潛在規劃能力，而不是沿著單一能力光譜的差異。我們在ACPBench-Hard上研究這個問題，通過在不同的測試時間推理預算下評估多個LLM家族，並應用多維項目反應理論模型來揭示潛在的LLM規劃能力結構。分析顯示塑造規劃表現的兩個主要維度：操作推理，即評估局部行動適用性和即時狀態轉變的能力，以及結構列舉，即推理目標可達性和地標結構的能力。操作推理在模型擴展和更長推理痕跡下有所改善，而結構列舉則相對不敏感。我們的發現促使對LLM規劃進行能力層級的評估，將重點從模型是否整體改善轉向哪些規劃能力改善、在什麼條件下改善以及為什麼。
